messages:
Marco (Acme): Hey — just cutover to our private VPC + customer-managed gateway and we start getting intermittent 429s from Redwood during traffic spikes. Only happens when we burst (bursty inference calls from our frontend). Not obvious in our app logs, but gateway shows a lot of `rate_limited` responses. Root request ts: 1919008405.

Marco (Acme): Example curl that gets 429 sometimes:
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"model":"gpt-4o-mini","input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
```
Response headers include `x-rate-limit-reason: local_token_bucket` and body `{"error":"rate limit exceeded"}`.

Ava (Support): Sorry you're hitting this — thanks for the detail. A couple quick Qs: are you running a customer-managed gateway in front of Redwood's Private control plane (so your Envoy -> our gateway -> Redwood), or is traffic going straight to our Private ingress? Also do you have any k8s ingress annotations for rate limit?

Marco (Acme): We have our Envoy (customer gateway) that forwards to the Redwood private endpoint in our VPC. In k8s the ingress uses `contour` and we set an annotation for a per-minute throttle. We also added an Envoy filter at the gateway level for local rate limiting. Config snippet we deployed: 
```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  annotations:
    projectcontour.io/max-request-body-size: 1m
    ingress.kubernetes.io/ratelimit: "60"  # requests per second per client ip (old annotation)
spec:
  rules: ...
```
And on the gateway we added an Envoy local rate limit: 
```yaml
local_rate_limit:
  token_bucket:
    max_tokens: 80
    tokens_per_fill: 20
    fill_interval: 1s
```

Diego (eng-runtime): Two quick observations from past escalations — when customer-managed gateway has local rate limiting AND k8s ingress/controller also enforces a bucket you can double-throttle. If the gateway uses client IP keying but the ingress is preserving client IP differently (or not), token buckets don't line up and you'll see bursts getting dropped. Also if you have an external Rate Limit Service (RLS) + local buckets, check for mismatch in `fill_interval`/`max_tokens`.

Priya (eng-sre): Also check whether the X-Forwarded-For is preserved end-to-end. If envoy is terminating and then requests to Redwood appear to come from the gateway's node IP, per-IP buckets collapse and look like a single noisy client -> quick exhaustion. Run: 
```
curl -s 'http://<gateway-admin>:19000/stats' | grep local_rate_limiter
```
and look for `local_rate_limiter.allowed` / `local_rate_limiter.enforced` counters.

Marco (Acme): Good call — we definitely see gateway IP in Redwood logs sometimes. We tried increasing `max_tokens` to 200 and bumped `tokens_per_fill` but still saw 429s during a 30s burst test.

Ava (Support): Can you share the exact burst test you used? We often repro with `hey` or `wrk`. Example we use to mimic frontend burst behavior: 
```bash
# 30s burst flood with concurrency 250
hey -n 10000 -c 250 -z 30s -headers "Authorization: Bearer <KEY>" https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate
```
If you can run that from inside your VPC (same path as production) it helps.

Marco (Acme): Ran that from a bastion — got ~60% 200s, ~40% 429s. Attaching excerpt from Envoy admin stats that looked suspicious:
```
http.local_ratelimit.allowed: 12345
http.local_ratelimit.enforced: 4678
http.local_ratelimit.enforced_local_overflow: 2345
```

Diego (eng-runtime): That `enforced_local_overflow` number says local bucket is hitting capacity and rejecting tokens on overflow. Two options: 1) move rate limiting to a single orchestrated RLS (Redis-backed) so edge local serves as small smoothing only, or 2) increase token_bucket `max_tokens` and `tokens_per_fill` to cover your 95th percentile burst delta. Also set `failure_mode_allow: true` on external RLS so a transient RLS outage doesn't hard-fail requests.

Priya (eng-sre): Another important config — the `stat_prefix` used by Envoy's local rate limiter must be unique per logical listener if you want separate buckets per route. If you reuse the same `stat_prefix` or key extractor, you end up sharing tokens across many routes. Also check `key_generator`: are you using `remote_address` or `header(x-forwarded-for)`? If the latter and header not present you get fallback to node IP.

Marco (Acme): We were using `remote_address`. How do we avoid IP collapse?

Priya (eng-sre): Ensure you have `use_remote_address: false` in your ingress controller config and preserve `x-forwarded-for` from client -> gateway -> Redwood. For contour/Envoy, set `use_proxy_proto` or proper `preserve_host` depending on chain. If proxy protocol is in play, make sure all hops understand it.

Ava (Support): TL;DR/checklist for you to try (low-risk first):
- Verify X-Forwarded-For is present in requests arriving at Redwood.
- Temporarily disable local rate limiting on gateway to confirm double-throttle.
- If you need local smoothing, increase token_bucket `max_tokens` to cover your observed 30s burst.
- Consider central RLS with Redis and enable `failure_mode_allow`.
- Run `hey` from inside VPC to reproduce and capture Envoy admin stats + Redwood rate limit counters.

Diego (eng-runtime): Sample Envoy local rate limit config we recommend for smoothing (adjust numbers to your burst pattern): 
```yaml
typed_config:
  "@type": type.googleapis.com/envoy.extensions.filters.http.local_ratelimit.v3.LocalRateLimit
  stat_prefix: http_local_rate_limiter_app
  token_bucket:
    max_tokens: 500        # allow short heavy bursts up to 500 tokens
    tokens_per_fill: 100  # refill 100 tokens per second
    fill_interval: 1s
  response_headers_to_add:
    - header:
        key: x-rate-limit-reason
        value: local_token_bucket
```
But if you need global enforcement (quota across many gateway replicas) use the external RLS + Redis.

Marco (Acme): Sounds good. One more thing — do we need to change anything on the Redwood Private side? We saw an `x-rate-limit-reason: local_token_bucket` from them as well.

Ava (Support): There are two possibilities: 1) Redwood's Private dataplane is applying its own per-tenant token bucket (we do that to protect the shared runtime), or 2) it's surface-level indication from your gateway. I'll check your account config and our Private side counters now; can you paste a request id from a 429 you collected?

Marco (Acme): Request-id: rwd-8c1f2a3d. Got it in the response body.

deploy-bot: Notifying eng-runtime on thread rwd-8c1f2a3d

Diego (eng-runtime): I pulled the trace for rwd-8c1f2a3d — it's showing enforcement at the Private dataplane layer. We currently apply a per-tenant soft limit + local bucket to protect the node. It looks like your gateway bursts + our tenant soft limit are interacting. Two practical fixes: raise your tenant commit (if you want guaranteed throughput) or configure your gateway to smooth spikes so you stay under the commit.

Priya (eng-sre): If you want to avoid raising commit immediately, try these quick mitigations: increase `max_tokens` on your gateway to match the burst, add a small queueing proxy (3s) to smooth bursts, or implement a client-side jitter/retry with exponential backoff (we see many frontends re-try aggressively and that multiplies burst effects).

Marco (Acme): We'll try disabling local RL on the gateway and run the `hey` test again, then report results. If that reduces 429s we can tune buckets rather than change commit.

Ava (Support): Great — please paste the envoy admin stats + `hey` summary when you have them. If disabling reduces 429s, we'll coordinate to help you roll a tuned token bucket config. If it doesn't, we'll escalate to the Private infra team to look at tenant-side enforcement values. :+1:

Marco (Acme): Will do. Thanks all. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:

Ava (Support): Marking ticket P3 -> we'll keep this open until resolved. Scheduling a short screen-share for 1919009200 if needed. :calendar:
